question: What is the primary danger of relying entirely on out-of-pocket health payments in poor communities?

options.A: Delayed medical care and catastrophic household poverty
options.B: Immediate free treatment for chronic infectious diseases
options.C: Overstaffing of rural community health clinics
options.D: Excessive funding of primary health care facilities

explanation: Paying cash directly for every service forces families to delay seeking help until conditions become severe, often wiping out their savings in the process. [learn more](GST322_U4_T4#GST322_U4_T4_h1)

question: Why is spreading financial risk important in community health care financing?

options.A: It ensures that healthy individuals never contribute money to clinics
options.B: It cushions individuals from the heavy financial shock of sudden illness
options.C: It eliminates the need for nurses to manage patient records
options.D: It allows the government to completely stop funding public hospitals

explanation: Pooling resources means the healthy subsidize the sick, protecting any single family from going broke due to unexpected medical emergencies. [learn more](GST322_U4_T4#GST322_U4_T4_h1)

question: What defines a Community-Based Health Insurance scheme?

options.A: Mandatory tax deductions enforced strictly by the federal government
options.B: Free medical care funded entirely by foreign manufacturing companies
options.C: Voluntary risk-pooling managed locally with regular member premiums
options.D: Daily cash payments made only when a patient is admitted

explanation: CBHI relies on community members organizing themselves voluntarily to pool regular contributions for shared health risks. [learn more](GST322_U4_T4#GST322_U4_T4_h2)

question: A local farmers association pays a fixed monthly sum to the nearby health center to cover malaria treatment for all members. Which financing model is this?
explanation: Paying a fixed amount in advance to secure care before an illness occurs represents a prepaid or retainer arrangement. [learn more](GST322_U4_T4#GST322_U4_T4_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of regular financial reports in community health insurance schemes?

options.A: To reduce the clinical workload of primary health nurses
options.B: To determine the salaries of international donor agencies
options.C: To apply for international loans from the World Bank
options.D: To maintain community trust and encourage continuous enrollment

explanation: Openly sharing financial records reassures members that their contributions are safe and being used strictly for health care. [learn more](GST322_U4_T4#GST322_U4_T4_h3)

question: How does a registered member access care under a functional community insurance scheme?

options.A: By waiting for annual free medical outreaches sponsored by politicians
options.B: By traveling to the state capital for specialized tertiary hospital admission
options.C: By presenting a membership card at the clinic for treatment and service reimbursement
options.D: By paying cash for drugs and claiming a refund from the police

explanation: Possession of the scheme membership card validates coverage, allowing the facility to treat the patient and draw funds from the pool. [learn more](GST322_U4_T4#GST322_U4_T4_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical role of nurses in community health financing?

options.A: Educating patients on the benefits of health insurance schemes
options.B: Maintaining accurate treatment records to prevent insurance fraud
options.C: Approving national macro-economic fiscal policies and tax rates
options.D: Assisting with the identification of vulnerable households for waivers

explanation: National macroeconomic policies and tax legislation are handled by government fiscal authorities, not clinical nurses. [learn more](GST322_U4_T4#GST322_U4_T4_h4)

question: Why is nurse involvement in community sensitization vital for health financing?

options.A: Nurses are legally mandated to audit commercial banks holding community funds
options.B: Nurses determine the profit margins of pharmaceutical drug suppliers
options.C: Nurses possess trusted community standing and can effectively explain scheme benefits
options.D: Community members will refuse to pay contributions unless collected by doctors

explanation: Because community members respect healthcare providers, nurses can easily clear up misconceptions and encourage enrollment. [learn more](GST322_U4_T4#GST322_U4_T4_h4)

question: What misconception do some healthy contributors often hold about health insurance pools?

options.A: They demand cash refunds if they do not fall sick during the payment period
options.B: They assume insurance covers all international travel medical expenses
options.C: They believe the government will pay double their contributions with interest
options.D: They expect free housing alongside medical treatments

explanation: A common misunderstanding among beginners is treating health insurance like a savings account or lottery rather than shared risk protection. [learn more](GST322_U4_T4#GST322_U4_T4_h5)

question: How does poor drug availability at a primary health clinic affect community health insurance?

options.A: It destroys trust in the scheme, causing members to stop paying premiums
options.B: It encourages members to utilize private tertiary hospitals more frequently
options.C: It forces the federal government to increase health sector funding
options.D: It builds stronger community resilience and resourcefulness

explanation: If members pay premiums but still cannot get basic medications at the clinic, they will view the insurance as a scam and drop out. [learn more](GST322_U4_T4#GST322_U4_T4_h5)

question: Which national funding instrument helps subsidize care for vulnerable populations in Nigeria?
explanation: The Basic Health Care Provision Fund (BHCPF) is specifically designed to extend primary health care services to the poor and vulnerable. [learn more](GST322_U4_T4#GST322_U4_T4_h6)

question: A rural health committee wants to make premium collection easier for farmers who lack bank access. What strategy should they adopt?

options.A: Use mobile money agents and simple digital payment platforms
options.B: Demand payment strictly in foreign currencies at commercial banks
options.C: Require patients to travel to Abuja for manual registration
options.D: Stop collecting cash and rely entirely on foreign donor grants

explanation: Mobile money and digital tools bridge the banking gap in rural areas, making financial transactions convenient for community members. [learn more](GST322_U4_T4#GST322_U4_T4_h6)
